title: What $100 a Month Becomes in 5 Years (Savings vs. Credit Card)

lines.say: A hundred dollars a month, for five years.
Where you point it changes the ending completely.

scene.label: $100 × 60 months
scene.sub: the starting point: just the money itself

lines.cap: Five years is 60 months, so that's $6,000 of your money either way.
lines.say: Five years is sixty months, so that's six thousand dollars of your money, either way.
Let's follow it down two roads, with real numbers.
Road one. A high-yield savings account.

scene.label: $100 a month at 4% for 5 years
scene.sub: $630 of that is interest you earned

lines.cap: Put $100 a month into savings earning 4%, and after five years you have $6,630.
lines.say: Put a hundred dollars a month into savings earning four percent, and after five years, you have sixty-six thirty.

lines.cap: $630 of that is interest the bank paid you. Rates change; 4% is our example.
lines.say: Six hundred and thirty of that is interest the bank paid you. Savings rates change over time, so four percent is just our example.
Road two. The same hundred dollars a month, but you're paying down a credit card.

scene.label: Credit card balance · 24% APR
scene.sub: interest: about $80 a month at the start

lines.cap: Say it has $4,000 on it at 24%. That's about $80 of interest in the first month alone.
lines.say: Say it has four thousand dollars on it at twenty-four percent. That's about eighty dollars of interest in the first month alone.
So of your hundred-dollar payment, only twenty actually goes to the balance.

lines.cap: After five years, you've paid $6,000, and you still owe $1,719.
lines.say: After five years, you've paid six thousand dollars, and you still owe seventeen nineteen.

lines.cap: $3,719 of what you paid went to interest. Paying it off fully takes 82 months: almost seven years.
lines.say: Thirty-seven nineteen of what you paid went to interest. Paying it off completely takes eighty-two months. Almost seven years.
Now put the two roads side by side.
Savings earned you six hundred and thirty dollars.
The card cost you thirty-seven nineteen.

scene.text: Paying off a 24% card is a guaranteed 24% return.

lines.say: That's why paying off a twenty-four percent card is like earning a guaranteed twenty-four percent. No savings account comes close.
So here's what happens if you find a second hundred dollars.

lines.cap: At $100 a month: 82 months and $4,128 in interest.
lines.say: At a hundred a month, eighty-two months, and forty-one twenty-eight in interest.

lines.cap: At $200 a month: gone in 26 months, for $1,159.
lines.say: At two hundred a month, it's gone in twenty-six months, for eleven fifty-nine.

scene.label: Then send the same $200 to savings
scene.sub: saved by year five, with the card already gone

lines.cap: Then flip the same $200 into savings for the rest of the five years. You end with $7,188 saved, and no card.
lines.say: Then flip that same two hundred into savings for the rest of the five years. You end with seventy-one eighty-eight saved, and no card.
Versus still owing seventeen nineteen on the slow road.
And if you're debt-free already, here's what small amounts become in five years.
Twenty-five a month, sixteen fifty-seven.
Fifty, thirty-three fifteen.
A hundred, sixty-six thirty.
Two hundred, thirteen thousand, two sixty.
